Produce a pixel-art SIDE CUTAWAY of an OPEN DOWNWARD MAINTENANCE SHAFT, matching the attached exact geometry guide (image1) and game's screenshot materials (image2). Nothing bridges the opening at its top: NO horizontal crossbeam, NO arch, NO door header, NO grille, NO gate, NO ladder, NO well roof, NO hanging ropes. It must be unmistakably a hole that a player drops into, not a door one walks through.
Draw a modest flush old gray-blue stone collar on the inner edge of each bank, just below ground level. Left stone facing occupies x330..426, right x1109..1205. Stone facing and short moss tufts blend into small dark earthen edge fragments towards each outer bank, fading to transparent outside x250..1285, no giant floor or platform illustration. Use hand-hewn weathered stone of the windmill, a few subtle rusty bronze anchor bolts, sparse olive moss at upper edges. Side walls do not lean into or narrow the passage. The actual terrain side faces are x426 and1109 and must remain clear.
Inside the open shaft BELOW y360 draw a recessed dark desaturated blue-slate masonry back wall, visibly behind the play plane, becoming darker toward the bottom. NO sky inside underground shaft. Back wall at x426..1109 with a subdued upper edge at ground level that does not look like a solid cap. Very subtle cool upper reflected light on inner side edges to show depth. It is a side-scrolling 2D section, no circular front-facing well ellipse, no floor at bottom. No bright light source or decoration in central playable air. Foreground lips two separate banks only.
Match the screenshot's fine clustered pixel-art character/world scale, restrained material contrast, earthy blue-gray stone and olive moss. Not photorealistic or painterly. Crisp edges at final native small size. Remove all guide colors, letters and arrows. This is one aligned transparent asset containing both shaft-side junctions and recessed back wall, to composite with existing terrain at exact supplied coordinates.
